title: The Uniform of Port Mahon
premise: In 1789 Port Mahon, Ada Joubert has spent her life in her father's print shop, learning that the safest words are the ones never set in type. When revolutionary soldiers requisition the town and seize the shop's ledger of names, Ada discovers her father secretly printed pamphlets for the resistance — and that Lieutenant Étienne Vasseur, the officer billeted with them, is the boy she loved a decade ago. Torn between protecting her family and finishing the forbidden printing run hidden beneath the floorboards before the century turns, Ada must choose which silences to keep. She completes the run at terrible cost — her father is arrested but escapes by sea, Étienne deserts rather than name names, and Ada inherits both the shop and the found family of printers who will carry the truth into the new century.
about_author: Yara Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing provincial print shops of revolutionary France. She writes historical fiction about the quiet people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Ada Joubert's POV. On an ordinary morning in the print shop, Ada sorts type while her father receives a stranger's sealed package he burns unread. The town hums with rumors of requisition. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — Ada notices what her father refuses to say, establishing her fluency in silence.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The army arrives; Lieutenant Étienne Vasseur is billeted in the Jouberts' attic, and Ada recognizes him as the apprentice who left ten years ago after a stolen kiss and a broken promise. He confiscates the ledger of names. Emotional beat: shock and old grief colliding with present danger.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. Sorting confiscated papers, Étienne finds coded marginalia matching pamphlets he once helped set as a boy. He says nothing to his superiors. Emotional beat: duty at war with memory — he realizes the girl he loved may be entangled in sedition.

chapters.title: Beneath the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada discovers her father's hidden press and half-finished pamphlet run for the resistance network. He confesses everything and asks her to finish it if anything happens to him. Emotional beat: betrayal transmuted into fierce, terrified love.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Looks Away
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Small truces form: Étienne covers for a missing crate of type; Ada mends his uniform coat without being asked. The other officers grow suspicious of the shop's comings and goings. Emotional beat: tenderness rekindling inside mutual deception.

chapters.title: Names in the Compositor's Hand
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Working nights, Ada sets the remaining pages, memorizing the names of resisters she'll never meet — a widow, a fisherman, two deserters hiding in the cistern. They begin gathering at the shop. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around shared risk.

chapters.title: The Denunciation
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. A rival officer denounces the print shop; Étienne is ordered to search it thoroughly at dawn. He warns Ada with a misquoted line of type only she would understand. Emotional beat: the point of no return — he chooses her over his commission.

chapters.title: Dawn Raid
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The raid comes; soldiers tear up the shop but find only fresh bread and a repaired press. Her father is arrested on older charges. Ada, pressed against Étienne in the dark stairwell, feels the cost of every silence they've kept. Emotional beat: climax of fear — victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. Étienne falsifies transfer papers, freeing Ada's father onto a boat bound for Algiers, then burns his own commission. He and Ada pull the final sheets of the pamphlet run as church bells ring out the old year. Emotional beat: love consummated through action, not words.

chapters.title: A New Century, Set in Type
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, one year later. The shop reopens under Ada's name; the resisters have become her household, and the pamphlets circulate farther than her father ever dreamed. A letter arrives from Algiers; a familiar coat appears at the door. Emotional beat: resolution — memory kept, silence broken, family made by choice.
